concepts.def: A consensus theory that views society as a system of interconnected parts working together to maintain stability, each institution performing a useful function.
A conflict theory arguing society is divided between a ruling capitalist class (the bourgeoisie) and the working class (the proletariat), with the economy shaping society.
A conflict perspective that examines how society is patriarchal and unequal between genders, seeking to explain and challenge women's disadvantage.
A micro approach focusing on small-scale, face-to-face interaction and the meanings and labels people attach to behaviour in everyday life.
Consensus theories such as functionalism stress shared values and order, while conflict theories such as Marxism and feminism stress division and inequality.
The patterned, relatively stable arrangements of institutions and relationships, such as family, education and class, that shape individual behaviour.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Sociological Theories & Approaches — a core area of GCSE Sociology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Sociological Theories & Approaches brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Sociological Theories & Approaches.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

options: In constant conflict
A system of parts working together for stability

Having no institutions

mcqs.q: Marxism argues the main division in society is between:
options: Men and women
The ruling class and the working class
Young and old people
Town and country

mcqs.q: Interactionism is a 'micro' approach because it focuses on:
options: Whole societies at once
Small-scale, face-to-face interaction
The global economy
Large structures only

mcqs.q: Functionalism is best described as a:
options: Conflict theory
Consensus theory
Feminist theory
Micro theory

mcqs.q: Is functionalism a consensus or a conflict theory?
options: Only the family as an institution.
It rejects all social institutions.
It is a conflict theory like Marxism.
A consensus theory - it stresses shared values and social order.

mcqs.q: According to Marxism, what shapes society the most?
options: Shared agreement between all social groups.
The economy and the conflict between social classes.
Only individual face-to-face meanings.
Only the family as an institution.

mcqs.q: What is the focus of interactionism?
options: Small-scale interaction and the meanings people give to behaviour.
The large-scale structure of the whole economy.
Only the family as an institution.
It rejects all social institutions.
